text:
Maria: CI job `h100-inference-integ/fast-warmup` turned red on main, looks like OOM during warmup + kernel preemption logs. can someone take a quick look?

Maria: snippet from pytest log:```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.20 GiB (GPU 0; 80.00 GiB total capacity; 74.50 GiB already allocated)
[  +0.002s] H100: Kernel preemption detected: reason=TLB_FAULT
```

Ajay: thanks — which run id and image? any reproducible steps locally? :eyes:

Maria: run id 2026-03-17_14-12-38 (job url: https://ci/redwood/jobs/2026-03-17_141238) image: redwood/ci:2026-03-17-h100-quant. repro is flaky: unit test passes locally half the time when run with --repeat 50.

ci-bot: Automated note: job 2026-03-17_14-12-38 failed on node gpu-h100-17, driver 535.54, cuda 12.2. Logs archived: https://ci/redwood/artifacts/2026-03-17_141238/logs.tar.gz

Taylor: could be a preemption/regression after driver bump. did we change kernel flags or enable preemption handling in runtime recently? pinging @Ajay for the runtime change on 2026-03-10. :thinking_face:

Ajay: I did land a small change to kernel launch flags (reduced shared mem alignment) on 2026-03-10, but it was gated. I will check the rollout window. can we collect a full dmesg + nvidia-smi output and try a single-test rerun with MALLOC_TRIM_THRESHOLD_=0 to avoid fragmentation?

Maria: grabbing dmesg and nvidia-smi from node now, will attach. quick nvidia-smi snapshot:```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 535.54       Driver Version: 535.54       CUDA Version: 12.2     |
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
|  0  H100-PCIE-80GB      On    | 00000000:3D:00.0 Off |                  N/A |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes:                                                       GPU Memory |
|  PID   Type   Process name                             Usage      |
| 12345    C   python                                      74512MiB   |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

Liam: if the process already holds ~74GB, warmup OOM makes sense. can you re-run with reduced batch size or enable our local kv-cache warmup throttle (set env REDWOOD_WARMUP_THRESHOLD=0.6)? also capture /sys/kernel/debug/dri/* for preemption traces.

Maria: re-run requested with smaller batch + MALLOC_TRIM... initiating rerun now: https://ci/redwood/jobs/2026-03-17_141358 (rerun id). will attach new logs when done.

Ajay: while rerun runs, can you also try a reproducer with the same image but GPU pinned to a smaller fraction (cgroup limits) or run with --no-cuda-graph? those often change memory layout and can expose fragmentation.

Taylor: if rerun still fails, file a bisect request and mark it high priority; we should try to bisect kernel launch flags change vs driver variant. I can help with the bisect script. :+1:

ci-bot: Rerun 2026-03-17_14-13-58 queued on node gpu-h100-05. Notifying on completion.

Maria: rerun passed with batch halved and REDWOOD_WARMUP_THRESHOLD=0.6. interesting — baseline still flaky on main though. will push a short PR that reduces default warmup concurrency and include the env toggle in tests to stabilize CI.

Ajay: sounds good. please include a follow-up issue to bisect kernel-launch change vs driver 535.54 if we see more hits. thanks for the fast triage everyone. :tada:
